conversation:
Alex: Heads-up — kernel LTS backport + nvlink driver update landed in staging. Need a planned rolling reboot in eu-west3 tonight to pick it up.

Priya: ETA on the window?

Alex: Targeting 00:30-03:30 UTC. Canary first (3 nodes), then 5-node waves. Expect short reconnections for long-lived grpc streams; KV cache persistence should survive but MIG contexts may re-create — warmup needed.

Marco: What services are the highest risk? model-serving, redis proxy, or kubelet/cni restarts?

Alex: Primary risk: GPU device reinitialization (nvidia module), MIG controller restart. kubelet will restart on node reboot so pods will be rescheduled. redis/etcd unaffected but tcp sessions will get torn briefly.

Emma: Can we avoid killing active in-flight generation jobs? We have high-priority canaries running until 01:00 UTC.

Alex: Plan: mark canary label, drain with pod-disruption-budget honouring, and scale ephemeral pools to absorb in-flight. Command we'll use:
```
kubectl label node $CANARY_NODE redwood/maintenance=canary
kubectl drain $CANARY_NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m --grace-period=120
```
Then run reboot script and validate device nodes exist:
```
ssh node && sudo systemctl restart nvidia-device-plugin
nvidia-smi -L && nvidia-smi topo -m
```

Li: How are we handling routing for requests that would hit draining nodes? Can we pre-warm another pool?

Alex: Yes — we'll temporarily add capacity to gpu-surge-2 (paid burst pool) and route new allocations there. We'll also set a fallback policy in the router to serve lower-cost model variant if latency SLOs start to slip:
- route: eu-west3 -> [primary-pool, gpu-surge-2]
- fallback: model-v1.large -> model-v1.medium

Priya: Cost estimate for burst pool?

Marco: Ops ran numbers: ~3 hours x 20 GPUs ~ 60 GPU-hours. With our burst pricing that's ~€420-€600. Set aside Ops wallet: COST-1004.

Emma: Any post-reboot regression checks we should run for model quality? We saw transient quantization state differences once before.

Alex: We'll run the standard post-deploy evals on a small prompt set (10 prompts) and check latency/cost deltas. Script:
```
# post-reboot smoke
curl -s https://eu-west3-api.redwood.internal/health
python infra/evals/run_eval.py --suite quick-smoke --targets model-v1.large
```
If eval fails, rollback: re-route traffic to gpu-surge-2 and open incident.

Li: Can we stagger reboots by rack to avoid cross-rack egress saturation? Bandwidth will spike during bulk cache warmup.

Alex: Yes — wave plan is rack-aware. We'll wait 15m between waves, and monitor egress bits via grafana panel `net.egress.eu-west3`.

OpsBot: Reminder: annotation required. Use command `@opsbot annotate maintenance:kernel-nvlink-5201122334` after scheduling.

Priya: Who's owning canary verification and rollback authority?

Emma: I'll own canaries and initial smoke. Marco will own wave 2+, Alex is on-call for infra kernel issues.

Marco: If any node shows nvlink errors after reboot run `dmesg | grep -i nvlink` and paste logs here. Also collect `/var/log/nvidia-device-plugin.log`.

Alex: Communication plan: post a short notice in #general-alerts 30m before start and update @customers-support with potential degraded capacity. We'll mark maintenance in the console page as well.

Li: Timeline recap:
- 00:00 UTC: final canary readiness check
- 00:30 UTC: canary drain + reboot (3 nodes)
- 01:00 UTC: canary smoke and eval
- 01:15 UTC: wave 1 (5 nodes)
- 01:35 UTC: wave 2 (5 nodes)
- 02:00 UTC+: remaining racks, 15m gap per wave, finish by ~03:30 UTC

Emma: I'll post progress updates in this thread and add short logs after each wave.

Priya: Approved. I'll notify on-call support around 00:15 UTC.

Alex: Thanks — tagging checklist: @opsbot annotate, scale up gpu-surge-2, set router fallback, canary label nodes, run the drain commands. See you all online at 00:20 UTC for preflight.

Marco: FYI: I'll keep an eye on billing alerts — set a soft threshold at +30% for the ops pool.

Emma: preflight note: run `kubectl get pods -o wide -l service=model-serving | grep Terminating` before we start to ensure no already stuck pods.

Alex: Last call for concerns. If nothing else, we proceed with schedule. :white_check_mark:
